bifrost: springboard/src/net/share.rs (Service, Peers, beacon, transfer), springboard/src/shell/share/glue.rs, springboard/sdk/src/share.rs
summary: BifrOSt has nearby LAN discovery and one-shot file and byte transfer between devices, run by the shell (UDP beacon on 224.0.0.251:5354, TCP transfer with an explicit Accept). Apps get no SDK API for peers, sessions, invitations or messages, and nothing is encrypted in transit; the MultipeerConnectivity session model is not covered.

features.note: Discovery runs in the shell over a fixed beacon group. Apps cannot browse by their own service type; there is no delegate for found or lost peers.

Wave 5 (w5-multipeer-connectivity, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The beacon carries a device name, a TCP port and a fingerprint of the shared secret. It is not per-app and apps cannot publish their own service.
The shell draws a Nearby device row and an incoming-offer prompt. No app can present the peer picker or receive the invitation decision.
A peer is a display name plus a socket address that changes with the network. There is no stable peer ID object an app can hold.

features.feature: Sessions and invitations (MCSession, invite and accept)
features.note: Wave 3 (theme-21, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Only a one-file Offer exists, answered by the user. There is no session object, no multi-peer connection state, and no connected or disconnected callbacks.

Wave 3 (theme-21, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. send_bytes sends a one-shot named payload from the shell. Apps have no send API and no reliable or unreliable mode.

File transfer works between BifrOSt devices with a size limit, a SHA-256 check and a receive deadline. There is no streaming API, no progress for apps (the shell passes a no-op progress callback), and apps cannot start it.

Wave 5 (theme-09, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The header carries an HMAC keyed by the secret, and the body is streamed in plaintext. No TLS or session encryption exists. The default secret is the constant "nearby".

features.feature: Background behaviour (stop and resume on background)
features.apple: framework stops advertising and browsing when the app is backgrounded
features.note: The shell owns the beacon and it runs while the desktop is up. Apps have no lifecycle hook for it.
Failures reach the shell as a text string. There is no typed error domain or code list.
Wave 3 (theme-21, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No session exists, so there is no peer limit.

gaps: No SDK API for peers: an app cannot browse or advertise its own service type, and cannot list nearby peers (springboard/sdk/src/share.rs exposes only show_picker and is_inbound).
No session model: no invitation flow, no connected and disconnected state, no multi-peer session object.
No app-facing message or resource send, and no streaming, so apps cannot exchange data with nearby peers.
No encryption in transit (body plaintext, HMAC over the header only) and a constant default secret "nearby".
No stable peer identity (MCPeerID); peers are a name and an address that changes.
The SDK share picker lists apps that accept the items and Copy, not the Send Nearby device list (per docs/bifrost-ui.md, Share sheet section).
